liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Bertha** (1 review): Bertha to Row Jimmy is very well played [23]
- **Foolish Heart** (1 review): Brent plays nice piano work around six minutes in, extending the song and showing its open-ended nature [25]
- **Scarlet Begonias** (1 review): The Scarlet-Fire performance made the reviewer dance in their seat and feel very happy [24]
- **Stella Blue** (1 review): Brent and Jerry create a rolling sequence, leading to a monumental, monster-sounding ending [16]

## The recordings

- **gd1988-06-28.sbd.skankweed.7802.shnf** (recommended): soundboard; 22 songs; 168 min; rated 3.25/5 by 4 [1]
- **gd1988-06-28.145612.ots.akg460.ackerman.miller.noel.t-flac16**: audience recording; 21 songs; 160 min [4]
- **gd1988-06-28.141703.OTS.AKG.Ackerman.Miller.Noel.t-flac2496**: audience recording; 21 songs; 160 min [5]
- **gd1988-06-28.fm-mtx.braverman.12187.sbeok.shnf**: matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 20 songs; 161 min; rated 4.75/5 by 4 [10]. Said about its sound: The ending features trumpets, flutes, drums, stars twinkling, horses thundering, and cannons shooting [16]
- **gd1988-06-28.110953.akg463.ackerman.Taraszki.flac16**: source not stated; 20 songs; 161 min; rated 4/5 by 3 [14]

## Around the show

- The reviewer recalls the show, people, crowd, fence, and music [18]
- The venue drew a great crowd, including many hot, young women [23]
- Victim and Foolish Heart were new songs at the time of this performance [23]
- The reviewer danced in pouring rain in front of huge speakers without seeing the band [26]
- The reviewer describes the location as a bad police state, not suitable for the Dead [27]
- Fire On The Mountain may even be better here than the Hampton 3.27 version [22]
- This is considered the strongest Foolish Heart to date, despite Jerry still working out the lyrics [25]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1988-06-28.sbd.skankweed.7802.shnf**: transferred by Skankweed; source: SBD>MC>DAT>CDR [1]. Also: Received in trade, ripped for abgd, then retracked by Charlie C. into something decent [17]
- **gd1988-06-28.145612.ots.akg460.ackerman.miller.noel.t-flac16**: taped by Ray Ackerman; transferred by Charlie Miller and Joe Noel; source: Ray Ackerman's Master Audience Cassettes; AKG 460 w/ck63 caps > AKG B18 phantom power unit > Sony D5 [4]. Also: Edited and mastered by Joe Noel using Audacity, resulting in a 16-bit 44.1 kHz FLAC file; Pauses and tape flips in set one were cross-faded during the editing process [4]
- **gd1988-06-28.141703.OTS.AKG.Ackerman.Miller.Noel.t-flac2496**: taped by Ray Ackerman; transferred by Charlie Miller and Joe Noel; source: Recording Info: Ray Ackerman's Master Audience Cassettes; AKG 460 w/ck63 caps > AKG B18 phantom power unit > Sony D5; Transfer Info: Master Cassettes (Sony… [5]. Also: Lineage confirmed by upgrading from shnid 132524 to shnid 110953, with thanks to Ray for masters [5]
- **gd1988-06-28.fm-mtx.braverman.12187.sbeok.shnf**: transferred by Peter Braverman; source: FM (matrix): DAT> CD> TrackThief> AIFF> Peak> WAV> SHN [10]. Also: Originally listed as SBD to DAT to CD, but identified as an FM source with DJ blather; The source contains a 15 KHz cutoff consistent with FM broadcasts, and the tracking was a mess [10]
- **gd1988-06-28.110953.akg463.ackerman.Taraszki.flac16**: taped by Recorded by Ray Ackerman; Conversion by Ray Ackerman; transferred by Tracks, FLACs, Tags by Craig Taraszki; source: AKG 460b/ck63uls > AKG B18> Sony TCD5; [14]. Also: Recorded from the front row balcony, with set one on the left center side; The second set was recorded from the right center side of the front row balcony [19]
